sec: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and CGM equipment

items.q: The treatment written below the dawn-phenomenon graph is:
items.exp: The dawn-phenomenon note gives increase night-time insulin dose. (Book p934)

items.q: Match the graph pattern to the page label — 1) Early-morning hyperglycemia without the 3 a.m. low 2) 3 a.m. hypoglycemia followed by morning hyperglycemia 3) Excess night insulin 4) Somogyi treatment … A) Dawn phenomenon B) Somogyi effect C) Midnight hypoglycemia D) Decrease night-time insulin dose
items.exp: The page labels the first graph dawn phenomenon, the second Somogyi effect, links excess night insulin to midnight hypoglycemia, and gives a decreased night dose as treatment. (Book p934)

items.q: Assess the Somogyi notes: I Counter-regulatory hormones are linked to early-morning hyperglycemia. II Excess nighttime insulin is linked to midnight hypoglycemia.
items.exp: Both arrows are written under the Somogyi graph. (Book p934)

items.q: A glucose tracing shows hypoglycemia at 3 a.m. followed by early-morning hyperglycemia. Which page label fits?
items.exp: The Somogyi graph explicitly marks hypoglycemia at 3.00 am followed by fasting hyperglycemia. (Book p934)

items.q: Which regular-insulin schedule is written under insulin regime?
items.exp: The insulin-regime line gives regular insulin 8–8–8. (Book p934)

items.q: Match the basal insulin option to the exact schedule — 1) Glargine 2) Degludec 3) Regular insulin basal option … A) 16 U at 11 PM daily B) 16 U on alternate night C) 16 U twice daily
items.exp: The page lists glargine 16 U at night daily, degludec 16 U on alternate nights and regular 16 U BD daily. (Book p934)

items.q: After insulin, base glucose is to be assessed how many times?
items.exp: The page says base glucose levels should be accessed 6 times. (Book p934)

items.q: The six base-glucose checks are pre- and post- breakfast, lunch and ___.
items.exp: The list specifies pre- and post-breakfast, pre- and post-lunch, and pre- and post-dinner. (Book p934)

items.q: Assess the dose-adjustment rule: I A dose may be increased by 2 units. II A dose may be decreased by 4 units.
items.exp: The final insulin-regime bullet gives increase by 2 units or decrease by 4 units. (Book p934)

items.q: Which item is labelled a component of the continuous glucose monitoring system?
items.exp: The CGMS diagram labels continuous glucose monitor, cable, glucose sensor and com-station; glucose sensor is one component. (Book p934)

items.q: Match the CGMS equipment label to its page description — 1) Sensor 2) Charger/com-station 3) Recorder 4) Inserter … A) Skin sensor B) Charging/display unit C) Recording device D) Insertion device
items.exp: The equipment drawings are labelled sensor, charger/com-station, recorder and inserter. (Book p934)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the two named overnight glucose patterns?
items.exp: Dawn phenomenon, Somogyi effect and fasting hyperglycemia appear in the overnight tracing notes; postprandial hypoglycemia does not. (Book p934)
